bib.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents

read.skipped: References skimmed only for lineage; no appendix in the paper.

question: Do software-engineering issue-resolution systems really need autonomous LLM agents, or does a fixed localize-repair-validate pipeline do as well?
hypothesis: A simple fixed pipeline without LLM-chosen actions or tools can match agent-based approaches at lower cost.
contributions: An agentless approach: hierarchical localization, multi-sample diff patches, reproduction and regression test based selection
Evaluation on SWE-bench Lite against 26 agent-based approaches plus ablations
SWE-bench Lite-S, a filtered benchmark of 249 problems after manual classification

method.summary: Agentless runs three fixed phases with GPT-4o: hierarchical localization (files, then classes/functions, then edit lines), sampling of Search/Replace patches, and patch selection using regression tests, an LLM-generated reproduction test and majority voting. The LLM never chooses actions or uses tools; all control flow is hand-written.

datasets.name: SWE-bench Lite
datasets.preprocessing: Official eval setup modified so arbitrary regression and reproduction tests can be run; PASS_TO_PASS list not used

datasets.name: SWE-bench Lite-S
datasets.split: Lite minus exact-patch, misleading-solution, and insufficient-info issues

inference.decoding: Greedy by default; sampling for extra candidates (1 greedy + n-1 sampled)
inference.samples: 4 edit-location sets per issue (sampled); 10 patches per set (1 greedy + 9 sampled) = 40 patches; 40 reproduction tests (1 greedy + 39 sampled). Single run per issue; no seeds stated.
inference.prompting: Zero/example-based prompts per step; reproduction test step gets one example test for format. Prompt text not in paper.
inference.retrieval: LlamaIndex, text-embedding-3-small, chunk size 512, overlap 0, cosine similarity; LLM first filters irrelevant folders; final files = top N common to prompting and embedding lists

parameters.normalisation: parse with Python ast, unparse, strip docstrings, diff old vs new
parameters.selection: fewest regression failures, then must print Issue resolved, fall back to regression only, then majority vote on normalised patches

metrics.name: % Resolved
metrics.definition: Share of benchmark problems whose submitted patch passes the benchmark tests

metrics.name: Avg. # Tokens
metrics.definition: Average input plus output tokens per issue

metrics.name: % Correct Location
metrics.definition: Patch edits a superset of the ground-truth locations, at line, function, file level

metrics.name: Contains GT
metrics.definition: Percent of problems whose ground-truth edit locations remain in the location set after a localization step

baselines: 26 agent-based approaches (SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover, Moatless, OpenDevin, Aider, SpecRover, CodeR, many closed-source)
RAG baseline with BM25 (SWE-bench) for GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude-2, Claude 3 Opus
eval.protocol: Baseline numbers taken from leaderboard or official papers, not rerun. One run, no variance or significance test reported.

limits: Data leakage of ground-truth patches into GPT-4o training data cannot be ruled out (authors concede, 7)
Only evaluated on SWE-bench family (Python issues); authors plan other benchmarks
Not the top overall: closed-source tools beat it on Lite (CodeStory Aide 43.00%)
Baseline numbers are copied from leaderboards; closed-source entries have no trajectories to verify
Reproduction tests are weak: 94 of 213 plausible; selection of the right patch leaves a gap to the 126 upper bound
Weaker than agents when the issue gives no location clue
Single run, no seeds or confidence intervals; no prompts given in the paper
Costs and rankings are from 2024 and with GPT-4o; leaderboard has since moved
Cost figures missing for most baselines (dash in Table 1)
Table 1 prints OpenCSG StarShip file-level 90.7% but text says 90.0%

terms.definition: an approach with a fixed three-phase process of localization, repair and patch validation, without letting the LLM decide future actions or operate with complex tools
a simple diff format with a search snippet (original code) and a replace snippet
a compressed file view listing headers of classes and functions (plus class fields, method signatures, class/module comments)
an LLM-written test that prints Issue reproduced, Issue resolved or Other issues
